verdict: A bounded fixed-type make/new subset is compatible with approved A01 intent, but a whitelist-only implementation is unsafe for the existing macro fragment contract.
approved_basis: RFC0011 lines11-15: capture categories and definition-site free-name binding, native evaluation dictated by template
RFC0011 line92: expression captures cannot be inserted into type positions
mvp-gap-audit A01: make/new remain engineering gaps; A02 general type fragments remain unfinalized
Existing sums.go fixedType plus primitive_bindings.go provide a conservative fixed-type precedent

probes.patch_scope: Go -overlay changes only two builtin whitelist expressions in hygiene.go; original repository is untouched
whitelist_failures: expr make type argument []int or caller Local accepted and executed
ident/tt make type argument caller Local accepted and executed
expr inside []$t accepted with caller int
expr new type argument caller Local accepted and executed
generic native .go declaration makes make(List[int]), make($t[int]) and new(List[int]) accept and execute
probes.existing_gap: Baseline already accepts ($t:expr)=>{func()$t{var v $t;return v}()} invoked with int. This is pre-existing expression-to-type leakage, not a make/new regression.
probes.positive: Fixed make slices/maps/channels and new scalar/composite types execute; caller-local int type does not capture the primitive; make length ? preserves source operand order and early return in a real Go race run.
probes.new_expression: new(expr) is native Go since1.26, already valid at repository go1.27; expression-only macro support requires type-vs-value validation so captures cannot name types. Child native-new/report.json contains 14native +5frontend controls.

minimum_gate: Identify actual definition-site builtin first, preserving template-local and real definition functions. Do not gate by callee spelling alone.

Before capture substitution require the complete builtin type operand to be a fixed AST composed of unshadowed predeclared type leaves, pointer/slice/literal-array/map/channel/parentheses as in existing fixedType; reject all capture placeholders at any depth.
Validate local AST binding identities as well as primitive spelling: template int:=7;new(int) is a legal value initializer, not a fixed type even though fixedType("int") alone says true.
Keep e.checkPrimitiveBinding collision checks and ResolveBuiltins package/local-type boundaries; preserve caller-local primitive shadow via aliases.
Do not accept unknown names, imported selector types, generic indexes or sum/helper aliases merely because generated prefixes are trusted.

Keep native arity/length/capacity/type errors, allocation and panic behavior; preserve ? frame/evaluation and ordinary callee shadows. Existing complete caller expression captures such as id!(make([]Local,2)) are still expressions and should remain allowed.
named_type_assessment: Fixed definition-site non-generic named type binding is consistent with existing free-name intent and is an engineering item, not inherently a new hygiene policy. Current Package stores topNames/funcs only, so it needs real type-identity, visibility and cross-file/package handling; it is not a two-line builtin subtask. Do not resolve names at caller by spelling or rename named types.
new_decision_boundary: Adding a general type fragment or allowing expr/tt/ident captures to act as types changes the current fragment contract; no such decision follows from make/new being on A01. new(expr) native value semantics are already established, but broadening the current macro implementation must prove captures remain values. A fixed-type-only slice should mark legal value forms as not-yet-implemented, never native-Go invalid.
fallbacks: Existing A01 expression-to-type leakage in syntactically explicit type slots can be fixed under the current rejection contract, with exact macro source diagnostics and no new syntax.
A03 direct-call atomic capture parentheses can be narrowly considered with AST context and raw/synthetic provenance preserved; do not globally remove parentheses.
scope: Research only. No repository edits, dependency installs, full-tree test runs, commits or pushes.
